all-on-empty.note: all() lowers to a SCORING subquery, not a plain NOT EXISTS. MAX over 2 (the body held) / 0 (it was false) / 1 (it was UNKNOWN) keeps the three CEL outcomes apart, and the NULLIF turns a 1 back into SQL NULL so an element whose `name` is missing denies the row under both polarities. A bare NOT EXISTS would read that element as 'did not falsify' and admit the row the PDP denies. COALESCE makes the empty relation score 0, which is all()'s vacuous truth.

cr-div-neg-zero.note: A division whose denominator may be zero is rewritten into IEEE arms rather than evaluated: the zero case becomes a constant arm, because CEL's `x / -0.0` is -Infinity where `x / 0.0` is +Infinity and SQL has neither value. That is what keeps a negative zero out of the bound parameters entirely — the sign of the zero decides an arm at translation time instead of reaching the database. Arithmetic composed ON such a division has no faithful arms and is refused instead (`cr-div-then-add`, #312).
